disposition_reason: Primary ICP-MS occurrence data for Pb, Cd, total As, Ni, Cr and Al in 38 Calabrian (Italy) apiary honeys, reported as mean/SD/median by floral variety in mg/kg wet weight.
disposition_locator: Section 2.2 (sampling); Table 2 (p. 5); Table 3 (p. 6); Section 3.1-3.2 and Figures 2-3 (pp. 6-8)

study.design: apiary sampling (occurrence survey with dietary risk assessment)
study.material_scope: Honey freshly collected from several beekeeping farms/apiaries in rural areas; five floral varieties: Wildflower (multifloral), Citrus, Chestnut, Honeydew, Erika (heather)
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Produced and collected at apiaries in Calabria, Italy (provinces of Catanzaro and Vibo Valentia); not purchased at retail. No purchase market.
study.collection_period: April to September (active beekeeping season); year not stated
study.method: ICP-MS (Agilent 7700x, ORS3) after microwave digestion (HNO3 5 mL + H2O2 1 mL, 0.5 g honey, Anton Paar Multiwave 3000) per UNI EN 13805:2002
study.lod_loq: LOD and LOQ 'ranged from 0.001 to 0.005 mg/kg' (3-sigma/10-sigma); per-analyte values not reported
study.basis: wet weight (as collected) - Tables 2 and 3 headed 'mg/kg w.w.'
study.qa: ISO 17025 validation; recovery at 0.005/0.05/0.5 mg/kg spikes, acceptance 90-110%, observed 96-105%; calibration r2 0.999 (0.05-10 ug/L, 7 standards); blanks; internal standards Sc, Y, In, Tb, Rh, Lu, Li, Ge, Bi. No CRM reported.

controls.control: Apiary siting relative to roads/traffic and intensive agriculture
controls.outcome: Authors attribute the elevated Pb (above the 0.1 mg/kg EU ML in many samples) to environmental pollution near apiaries in rural areas used for intensive agriculture and possibly influenced by vehicular traffic from nearby roads; Pb in honey attributed to airborne exposure of foraging bees. Not tested.

controls.control: Floral source / multifloral vs monofloral honey
controls.comparator: Wildflower (multifloral) vs Citrus, Chestnut, Honeydew, Erika
controls.outcome: Share of samples >0.1 mg/kg Pb: Wildflower 80%, Citrus 50%, Honeydew 50%, Chestnut 25%, Erika 25%. Authors suggest multifloral honey may be more exposed to inorganic contaminants. No significance test for Pb by variety reported.
controls.locator: Section 3.2 and Figures 2-3, pp. 7-8; Section 4 para 5, p. 12

controls.outcome: Authors note (citing literature ref [3]) that Al in honey can be influenced by aluminium equipment used in processing before marketing; not measured in this study.

controls.control: EU maximum level for Pb in honey (Regulation (EU) 2023/915, 0.10 mg/kg)
controls.outcome: Source states Pb exceeded the 0.1 mg/kg limit 'in most of the analyzed samples'. Applying the per-variety percentages to the stated n gives ~18.5 of 38 (~49%), and the Erika figure (25% of 6) is not an integer, so 'most' is not verifiable.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary repeats that Pb exceeded the EU ML in 'the majority of samples'; the per-variety percentages applied to the stated n give ~18.5/38 (~49%), and 25% of the 6 Erika samples is 1.5 samples - the claim is not reproducible from the primary.
Stored summary does not flag the Wildflower Pb median of 0.934 mg/kg printed in Table 2 (vs mean 0.125, SD 0.085), an apparent typo.
Stored summary does not flag that Fig. 3 shows ~50% of Erika samples <0.09 mg/kg Pb, which cannot be reconciled with the Table 2 Erika mean 0.104 +/- 0.004 mg/kg.
Stored summary lists internal standards as Sc, Y, In, Tb, Rh, Lu; the primary also lists Li, Ge and Bi (minor).
Stored summary's 'Key microelements' table omits Honeydew and Erika Ni/Cr/Al values and all medians (omission, not error); its means for the listed cells match the primary.
unresolved: Wildflower Pb median 0.934 mg/kg (Table 2) is implausible; true value unknown.

Erika medians for Table 3 (Ni 0.043, Cr 0.036, Al 5.031 mg/kg) come from a row displaced in the markdown conversion; assignment to Erika inferred from position/column order. No PDF in the library to verify.

Several Table 3 medians are far outside mean +/- SD (e.g., Honeydew Ni median 0.187 vs mean 0.086 +/- 0.023; Erika Ni median 0.043 vs 0.091 +/- 0.005; Citrus Cr median 0.018 vs 0.011 +/- 0.002); medians may be unreliable.
Chestnut As SD (0.011) exceeds its mean (0.003).
Per-sample values not printed; Pb exceedance percentages (Fig. 2/3) are only in charts, and the Erika percentage is inconsistent with n=6.
Calendar year(s) of collection not stated; only 'April to September'.
Per-analyte LOD/LOQ not reported (only a 0.001-0.005 mg/kg range), so lod_ug_kg left null.
Table 5 Pb EDI values are inconsistent across varieties (e.g., Wildflower 3.00e-6 vs Citrus 2.00e-4 mg/kg bw/day despite near-identical means); exposure figures not used here.
